standard_prerequisites: Flatness and weak associated points, and the criterion that a module is zero when it has no weakly associated point

The inclusion of the weakly associated points of a subquotient into those of the ambient module, and the containment of the weakly associated points of a flat finite type module in the associated points of the fibres
Faithful flatness of the map of local rings induced by a flat morphism at a point of the image, and the resulting injectivity of the base changed stalk
core_obligations: Reduce the base change assertion to the case of no base change by observing that the hypothesis on the associated points is preserved under base change
Let the kernel of the canonical map be considered, and reduce its vanishing to the emptiness of its weakly associated points
Bound the weakly associated points of the kernel by those of the module, and use flatness of the module over the base to contain the latter in the associated points of the fibres

For a point of the associated points of the fibres choose a preimage under the flat morphism, use faithful flatness of the map of local rings to see that the base changed stalk injects into the stalk at the preimage, and factor that injection through the canonical map to conclude that the kernel vanishes at the point
Conclude that the kernel has no weakly associated points, hence is zero, and that the same argument applies after any base change
proof_roadmap: Reduce to proving injectivity before base change using preservation of the hypothesis
Replace vanishing of the kernel by emptiness of its weakly associated points
Use faithful flatness at a chosen preimage of each associated point to kill the kernel point by point
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the universal injectivity of the canonical map to the pushforward along a flat morphism whose image contains the associated points of the fibres at source lines 1162-1174, label lemma-universally-separating, whose proof occupies source lines 1176-1214. The proof is a complete local argument rather than a citation: it reduces the base change assertion to its unbased version, passes from the vanishing of the kernel to the emptiness of its weakly associated points, bounds those weakly associated points by the associated points of the fibres using flatness of the module over the base, and then at each of those points chooses a preimage along the flat morphism and uses faithful flatness of the induced map of local rings to show that the base changed stalk embeds into the stalk at the preimage, an embedding that factors through the canonical map and therefore kills the kernel at the point. The counted statement records neither the weakly associated point reduction nor the faithful flatness step.
